solves: Shows data that the person reads and compares in rows and columns, with caption, header, cells and footer, and lets a row open its detail or the next level of a hierarchy.
use_when: To read and compare data in rows and columns, such as a statement, a report or a list of items.
framed for a table standing alone on the page; without the frame inside a card or panel, which already have a border.
A fixed header when the list is long inside a panel; horizontal scroll when the columns do not fit.
A two-level header to group columns of the same subject, such as accesses by channel.
An expanding row for the detail that does not fit in the row, such as an order and its items. It opens only through the chevron.
A tree, up to three levels, for a hierarchy, such as unit and sub-unit.
Size large on a touch screen or for a more relaxed reading; default otherwise.
do_not_use_when: To sort, select, filter or paginate: that is the nph-data-table.
To lay out the page: the table holds data.
With an empty cell when data is missing: use the no-value dash.
With numbers aligned to the start: align them to the end.
With an action written as a link: use the button in the cell.

size.constraint: The Figma property `size`. Default takes the row table/row-height and the cell sides table/cell-padding-inline; large takes table/row-height-large and table/container-padding, for touch or a more relaxed reading. Reflects because the internal CSS reads it. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

framed.constraint: The Figma property `moldura`. The border table/border in table/border-width with the corner table/radius, for a table standing alone on the page; the last row leaves its divider to the frame.

sticky-header.constraint: The Figma property `cabeçalho fixo`. The scroll area stops at table/body-max-height and the header stays while the body scrolls, with the line table/sticky-divider-* under it.

striped.constraint: The Figma `estado` `faixa`, for the whole table: every other row of data in table/row-striped-background. An expanded item does not count. On the host is a technical proposal of P97.

grid.constraint: The Figma property `grade`, for the whole table: the vertical line between the columns of the body, in table/border. On the host is a technical proposal of P97.

caption.constraint: The Figma `legenda` and `texto da legenda`: the title above the table, already localized. It is the accessible name of the table (aria-labelledby). Empty, there is no caption.

description.constraint: The Figma `descrição` and `texto da descrição`, under the caption title, in table/caption-foreground. It describes the table (aria-describedby). Only with a caption.

total.constraint: The Figma `total`: the text of an nph-badge secondary beside the caption title. Only with a caption.

label.constraint: The accessible name of a table without a caption. With neither, the table renders and emits console.warn once in development.

no-value-label.constraint: What the screen reader reads in the no-value dash, already localized, such as sem valor. Empty while a cell has no value, the dash is read as a dash and the table emits console.warn once in development.

empty-heading.constraint: The heading of the nph-empty that fills the body when rows is empty. Required then: without it the body stays blank and the table emits console.error in development.

empty-description.constraint: The description of the nph-empty of the empty body.

columns.constraint: Property only. Each column is key, header, align, group and width. key is unique and header names the column; align is start (default, text) or end (numbers, with tabular figures), and the header and the footer follow it; group puts a title above neighbor columns of the same group; width is the content width of the column, set in use. An empty list, a column without key or header, a repeated key or an align outside the two draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.

rows.constraint: Property only. Each row is key, cells, detail, children, open, loading and toggleLabel. cells maps a column key to a cell; detail opens the expanded item; children makes the next level of the tree, up to three; open says whether it starts open; loading spins the chevron; toggleLabel names the chevron. Opening a row replaces rows with a new list where that row has the new open. An invalid row is left out and emits console.error in development.

footer.constraint: Property only. A value per column key, such as the total, drawn with the background and the typography of the header. Without a value for any column, there is no footer.

default.choose_when: Otherwise: a screen with a pointer and a dense reading.

large.choose_when: On a touch screen or for a more relaxed reading.

framed.choose_when: A table standing alone on the page. Without it inside a card or panel, which already have a border.

sticky-header.choose_when: A long list inside a panel: the body scrolls and the column titles stay.

hover.changes_for_user: The whole row under the pointer takes the hover background.

striped.changes_for_user: Every other row of data takes the stripe background.

grid.changes_for_user: A vertical line separates the columns of the body.

focus.changes_for_user: The scroll area that overflows and the truncated text take the ring in table/focus-ring-width with the keyboard; in the tree, so do the focused row and cell.

open.changes_for_user: The chevron points down and the expanded item or the next level of the tree shows under the row.

loading.changes_for_user: A cell shows an nph-skeleton line in place of its content; a row that loads spins its chevron.

empty.changes_for_user: With no row, the body holds the nph-empty and the header stays visible.

business_rules: Text aligns to the start and numbers to the end, with the header and the footer of the column.
A missing value is the no-value dash, read as no-value-label; the cell is never left empty.
A truncated text carries a tooltip and the focus on the cell, and needs the column width.
With two actions or more, the frequent one stays visible and the rest go in the more, with Delete last.
The expanding row and the tree open only through the chevron, never by a click on the row; in the tree, the keyboard on the row opens and closes it too (P101). The tree goes down to three levels.
The caption names the table; without it, label does.
Sorting, selection, filtering and pagination belong to the nph-data-table.
ai_hints: Use nph-table to read and compare data; to sort, select, filter or paginate, use the nph-data-table.
Pass columns and rows as properties; give each row a unique key, which the events carry back.
Align a number column with align end; give a column a width when it carries truncated text.
Leave a missing value as null and set no-value-label to the text the screen reader reads, such as sem valor.
Give the table a caption, or a label when there is no caption.
Use the actions cell for Edit and more, the mixed-actions cell for a written Edit and more, and the button cell for one action; never a link for an action.
Listen to nph-row-action for the buttons of the cells and nph-row-toggle for the chevron; load children or detail on open and pass rows again.
Use framed for a table standing alone on the page, and sticky-header for a long list inside a panel.

accessibility.semantics: A native table in the shadow root: column headers with scope col, the group header with scope colgroup over its colgroup, the body and the footer. A table that draws a tree is a treegrid (P101): its cells are gridcells, each row carries aria-level, aria-posinset and aria-setsize, and a row that opens carries aria-expanded. The flat table stays a native table.
accessibility.accessible_name: The caption title (aria-labelledby), with the description as aria-describedby; without a caption, label. The icon-only buttons and the chevron carry a name per row, from the data.
keyboard: Tab reaches the scroll area when it overflows, and the arrows scroll it
Tab reaches the truncated text, which opens its tooltip
Tab reaches the links and the buttons of the cells and the chevron; Enter and Space activate the buttons
In the tree, Tab reaches one row and then the links, the buttons and the truncated text of that row only, and leaves the table

In the tree, on a row: Right opens a closed row or goes to its first cell, Left closes an open row or goes to its parent, Down and Up go to the next and the previous row, Home and End to the first and the last, Enter opens and closes

In the tree, on a cell: Right and Left move along the row, Left on the first cell goes back to the row, Down and Up keep the column, Home and End go to the first and the last cell, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to that column in the first and the last row
accessibility.focus: The scroll area that overflows and the truncated text take the ring focus/border in table/focus-ring-width with the keyboard, and so do the focused row and cell of the tree. The chevron, the buttons and the more use the focus of their own piece.
accessibility.contrast: Text and link pass AA over background, stripe, header and hover, in light and dark; the status icons pass 3:1. Exception accepted in the evidence: the rating star in table/rating-foreground is below 3:1 in light, and the score stays as a number beside it.
accessibility.color_alternative: The status has a shape and a name besides the color, the badge always has text, the link is underlined, and the no-value dash is read as text.

invalid_combinations: A size outside default and large — the table draws nothing.
No column, a column without key or header, a repeated key, an align outside start and end — the table draws nothing.
A row without key or with a repeated key, with both detail and children, with children at the third level, a row that opens without toggleLabel, a detail without name — the row is left out.

A cell type outside the list, a composite cell without its required text, a badge severity or a status outside the list, an icon outside the core, a link href with a protocol other than http, https, mailto or tel — the cell is drawn blank.
anti_patterns: Leaving a cell empty when data is missing.
Writing an action as a link.
Truncating text without the tooltip and the focus.
Using the table to lay out the page, or to sort, select, filter or paginate.

sources.design_md: design.md has no entry yet for the table/* tokens (pending decision D8 of DSA-49); they are in src/tokens/source/semantic.tokens.json
sources.decision: P97 — API and semantics of nph-table, 26-10-2026; P101 — the tree as a treegrid, 28-10-2026
